gates.body:
Decision needed: create the read-only service account so the dashboard can read Go usage windows.

Why it matters: the .env key is the Go INFERENCE key, proven 403 on all usage endpoints (2026-11-17). Only a console service-account key (or a browser-cookie session) can read the 5h/weekly/monthly windows. Extra Usage is OFF, so headroom reads literally once wired.

Steps (verified against dev.opencode.ai/docs/console/api):
1. Console > Settings > Service accounts > Add Service Account, name e.g. workbench-usage.
2. Open it > Add API Key, name e.g. usage-read.
3. Permissions: Restricted with Usage set to Read (tightest), or Read only. Expiry: Never (or 365d custom + rotation note).
4. Copy the key ONCE (shown once, oc_sk_... prefix afterwards).

Then paste it here as your answer (or add OPENCODE_USAGE_KEY=<key> to .env yourself). Do NOT overwrite OPENCODE_API_KEY. Read-only keys cannot call models; usage counts to the service account's own budget; revocable anytime.

Technical recommendation: Restricted + Usage/Read + Never expiry.
Question: paste the key, or say cookie-path.
gates.title: OpenCode: create usage-read service account

gates.body:
Decision needed: go/no-go on the bank-first trainer slice (first AI consumer of KnowMe facts).

Why it matters: storage + atomic ingest + grouped display are done and live; no consumer uses the bank yet. The slice wires trainer reads without changing ingest.

Options:
A: Build the first slice (recommend). Pro: proves the bank end to end; small, reversible. Con: one session of build/test.
B: Bank more facts first. Pro: richer data. Con: consumer design stays unvalidated.
C: Defer trainer entirely. Pro: focus elsewhere. Con: KnowMe stays write-only.

Technical recommendation: A.
Question: A, B, or C?
gates.title: KnowMe AI trainer: approve first slice?

Decision needed: how much to verify per-model capabilities in model_catalog.toml.

Why it matters: routing and fallback read these flags, but several are unmeasured declarations. A wrong flag misroutes real work.

Options:
A: Verify key routes by eval (recommend), scoped to installed Ollama + live hosted routes. Pro: ground truth. Con: model calls + harness slice first.
B: Trust declarations, verify on failure. Pro: zero upfront cost. Con: first failure hits real work.
C: Defer. Pro: nothing now. Con: routing confidence stays flat.

Technical recommendation: A.
Question: A, B, or C?
gates.title: Model-capability mapping: verify or trust declarations?

gates.body:
Decision needed: where Mai supervision lives and what it may do unattended.

Why it matters: the drain executes queued runs while the owner is away, but supervision is scattered (supervisor tick, probe, mail notify, boot reconcile) with no single authority for pause/kill/page.

Options:
A: Dashboard-native supervisor (recommend). Pro: single authority; tick + reconcile already there. Con: dashboard must run (supervised).
B: Mai-side supervision. Pro: closer to the work. Con: split authority; new protocol.
C: Keep scattered + document. Pro: nothing now. Con: gaps stay.

Authority sub-decision: pause-only, or pause + kill + page (needs mail-noise rules)?

Technical recommendation: A with full authority + mail-noise rules.
Question: A, B, or C — and pause-only or full authority?
gates.title: Mai supervision: placement, authority, paging?

gates.body:
Decision needed: unblock the company-site launch tracks or explicitly defer them.

Why it matters: shell + intake live, but launch is gated on deliberation: (1) public naming (R6; research on 'Company names' awaits CLOSE/RE-RUN), (2) offering details, (3) pricing.

Options:
A: Deliberate now, track by track (recommend starting with naming). Pro: unblocks the top product. Con: owner time.
B: Defer with a date. Pro: focus stays. Con: site stays a shell.
C: Park P7 entirely. Pro: clarity. Con: drops the client channel.

Technical recommendation: A for naming, B with a date for offering/pricing if full.
Question: A, B, or C — and if A, naming first?
